Eternal Night

Where nobody looks anymore, the night stays.

Not every part of the city gets looked at. Sealed doors, empty windows, a sign for a shop that closed years ago, a painting on a wall nobody walks past anymore. Where attention has withdrawn, the night stays, even at noon. This is the Eternal Night. It is not a place so much as a condition, and it is the one thing Terminal City works against. Not a villain. Just forgetting. When people stop noticing a room, a wall, a habit a neighbourhood had, the night settles into it and what was there goes missing, quietly. The Eternal Night keeps nothing. It only shows the city where it is losing. **Continuity.** After 08. This is the first evening, not the result of the final Fog in 12. Leaves a modest unfinished task for the second Meeting at the start of 15.

The new paint catches the last light. Behind it, the old doorway seems to have missed the afternoon entirely.

The bench painter and the Old One stand beside the sealed brick opening after the crows have gone east. At the front, the resident with the cup is telling someone about the music from upstairs. Neither person looks this far back.

Eternal Night gathers where attention has withdrawn. It does not need the whole city to become dark. An old sign, an unused room or a piece of wall can fall out of people's lives while the street around it stays busy. Nothing comes to take it. Fewer people have reasons to notice, until almost nobody does.

The painter puts a small mark across the doorway's worn edge. The brick becomes easier to distinguish. Nobody turns. She adds a second, brighter touch and waits. At the entrance, someone laughs at something the resident has said. Neither looks back. The painter studies the paint still on her brush.

The Old One holds out the brush rag. After a moment the painter takes it. The Old One brushes a little grit from the threshold. In the puddle below, there is no old route tonight, only the two workers and the new wall behind them.

They leave the mark in place. The courtyard already has music and somewhere to sit. Tomorrow they can give the eye a reason to travel farther. At the entrance, the painter looks back once. The corner is still there.

The ruleWhat nobody looks at is where the night lives.

Terminal City · Storybook v0.9.0 · built 2026-09-12
Terminal City is an original fictional mythology inspired by Vancouver’s geography, weather, wildlife, infrastructure, art, and electronic music. It makes no claim to historical, Indigenous, or religious tradition. Real places are used as settings; the operating system layered on them is invented.
Made by Steve Hiehn, a software developer and electronic musician based in Vancouver, Canada. All music was created using a custom DAW, Signals & Sorcery.
